text.paragraph: First visit to establish shared care for breast cancer on adjuvant tamoxifen, fourteen weeks after bilateral mastectomy and right axillary dissection. Concerns: Wants his breast cancer follow-up and tamoxifen managed close to home after his surgery and the start of tamoxifen at another hospital; Had not known that men could get breast cancer and dismissed his first symptom as aging or a strained muscle; wants to understand his risk of recurrence and what it means for his family. [S]

tr.td: Diagnostic mammography of both breasts: 1.9 cm irregular, spiculated retroareolar mass in the right breast (BI-RADS 5); left breast with no mass or gynecomastia (BI-RADS 1)

Ultrasound of both breasts and both axillae: 1.8 cm irregular hypoechoic retroareolar mass in the right breast; one right axillary lymph node with a thickened cortex; left breast and left axilla normal

Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the right breast mass and the right axillary node: invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 2; estrogen receptor 95 percent, progesterone receptor 80 percent, HER2 1+ (negative), Ki-67 15 percent; the node contains metastatic carcinoma
Bilateral mastectomy, at another hospital. Pathology: right breast, invasive ductal carcinoma 1.8 cm, grade 2, margins clear, no lymphovascular invasion; left breast, benign breast tissue
Right axillary lymph node dissection, at the same operation: 1 of 14 lymph nodes with a 4 mm metastasis, no extranodal extension; pT1c pN1a, stage IIA
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

tr.td: First visit to establish shared care for breast cancer on adjuvant tamoxifen, fourteen weeks after bilateral mastectomy and right axillary dissection
Four-week follow-up with medical oncology consultation: adjuvant plan, germline testing, tamoxifen safety, and bone density results
Three-month follow-up: germline result, tamoxifen side effects and adherence, vitamin D recheck
Survivorship visit: cancer-related history and examination, tamoxifen review, and written survivorship care plan
Medical oncology consultation to take over adjuvant endocrine therapy, confirm that no further adjuvant treatment is needed, and arrange germline genetic testing
Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for an initial five years, with venous thromboembolism symptoms, mood, hot flashes, sexual side effects, adherence, and interacting medicines reviewed at every visit
Genetic counseling and germline multigene panel testing (including BRCA2, BRCA1, PALB2, CHEK2, and ATM), with a letter for first-degree relatives explaining the result
Bone health: DXA at baseline, vitamin D repletion, dietary calcium, and weight-bearing exercise; bone-modifying drugs only for osteoporosis, not to prevent recurrence

Survivorship surveillance: cancer-related history and examination of both sides of the chest wall and both axillae every 3 to 6 months for 3 years, then every 6 to 12 months to 5 years, then yearly; no routine imaging, blood tests, or tumor markers without symptoms; lymphedema checks
Distress screening at each visit, at least 150 minutes of activity a week, and a written survivorship care plan
Take tamoxifen every day with side effects managed, aiming to continue for at least five years
No missed doses by pill count over seven months; mild hot flashes and a mild fall in libido, both manageable; no clot symptoms
Complete germline genetic testing with counseling, and give him written information for his relatives
No pathogenic variant in a multigene panel; family letter given
Establish bone health on hormone therapy at his age: DXA, vitamin D of 30 ng/mL or more, and weight-bearing exercise
Femoral neck T-score -1.2; vitamin D 36 ng/mL after supplementation
Give a written survivorship care plan with the surveillance schedule
Survivorship care plan given at the survivorship visit
